title: Book One · Chapter 49: A New Sign
story:
The oil shop changes its sign on a clear Thursday morning. Ronan looks at the wall. The old sign is gone. The new board leans inside the doorway.

A man is painting the new name in white. Dark blue paint covers the old name.

“Did the shop move?” Ronan asks Mum.

“No. The owner's brother is joining him. They're changing the name.”

Ronan looks at the door. The same oil jars stand behind it. The same step has a broken corner. The shop is in the same place. But his map has the old name. Someone may not find it from that name now.

At school, he tells Leo. Leo wants to keep the old name. He knows that name well.

“Someone new won't know it,” Ronan says.

“Someone old will.”

“Which name should we put?” they ask Miss Wu. She asks a different question. “Who needs your map?”

“People new to this street,” Ronan says.

“Those people need the new name. They can find the sign from it.”

At break, the boys add the new shop name. Mum wrote the new name on a slip. The boys copy it. They check each letter. Beneath it, in smaller letters, they put OLD OIL SHOP. They add the date of the change on the back.

“Put a blue square beside the name,” Mei says. “The sign is blue now.” Ronan gives her the blue pencil. Then he asks about her name. Does she want it beside this part?

“It's one square,” she says. “Put my name beside the colours.”

He writes it in the corner. Leo adds his name beside the station road. He drew most of that part. Ronan adds his own door and lane work. Their names take up most of the corner. Each person has a name beside the right part.

After school, Mum takes them to check the new sign. It is up now. The paint shines. The owner stands beneath it with a clean rag.

Ronan shows him the map. “Is this name right?” he asks. The man reads it slowly.

“Right name. Wrong door width. You make my shop look thin as a cupboard.”

“I can't fit all the real widths,” Ronan says.

The man smiles. “Fair enough. Just don't send customers through the cupboard.”

He points to a low closed building beyond the lane. It used to sell rice. It is empty now. The last owner left some time ago. People still call it the rice shop. The sign is faded. The boys cannot read its words clearly.

“Does that need a new name?” Leo asks.

“It is still the old rice shop for now. A new owner can choose a new name.”

They draw it as CLOSED OLD RICE SHOP. Ronan puts a little bar across its front door. There is a narrow passage behind it. Boards stand across the entrance. They cannot see much beyond them. They don't go through.

At home, Dad looks at the updated map. Dad points past the old rice shop. “Two more turns,” he says. “Then you reach Mr Sun's counter. It is on the main road.” They do not know the exact doorway yet. They put a question mark there. Dad can show them on another walk.

Mum puts the map beside her delivery notebook. Mum has a new customer's address. She reads it first. Then she looks for that place on the map.

Mum will still read the full address first. Ronan watches her check both papers. He checks their own green gate again. It has the full street name now, not just HOME. He shows the full name to Dad. Dad reads it and points to their gate. He does not need another question.

Before bed, he dates the lower corner. The paper is still the same paper. He puts the map back by the wall. The new names and dates are dry. Tomorrow Leo can check the new words and dates.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：sign＝招牌；name＝名字；closed＝关闭的；passage＝通道。

理解问题：

1. 旧招牌为什么会让街图失效？
2. 孩子们决定怎样保留旧信息，同时写清现在的情况？
